headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared repo/context handling; Copilot’s write-capable Workspace can amplify Airflow-fed content into edits.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can ingest and transform external content via broad network egress, while GitHub Copilot reads repo context and open buffers. That creates a plausible instruction-in-content bridge if Airflow outputs are copied into files or buffers Copilot consumes. No shared channel is documented, so this is not high, but the pathway exists in common workflows.
conditions: IF Airflow output is written into a repository file or editor buffer that Copilot reads
IF the content contains attacker-controlled instructions or prompt-like text
mitigations: Keep Airflow outputs out of Copilot-visible files
Review generated text before pasting into editor buffers
Use a separate scratch workspace for pipeline outputs
Disable Workspace apply for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between pipeline outputs and editor context

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers. If sensitive data is placed in shared files or buffers, Copilot may transmit that context to api.githubcopilot.com. Airflow’s touched data classes are unspecified, so uncertainty pushes upward from low to medium rather than downward.
conditions: IF sensitive data is present in files or buffers that Copilot indexes
IF Airflow writes secrets or regulated data into the same workspace
mitigations: Keep sensitive Airflow artifacts outside Copilot-indexed folders
Redact secrets before opening files in the editor
Use separate Git worktrees for data and code
Turn off Copilot for sensitive repositories
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data classification filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Airflow is an automation/data-orchestration system with broad network egress. In a shared repo, both can touch the same mutable resources, and Copilot’s per-editor isolation does not guarantee coordination with Airflow jobs. The overlap is real but not enough evidence for high because Airflow’s write surface is not explicit.
conditions: IF Airflow jobs and Copilot edits target the same repository or workspace
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while Airflow is generating or updating files
mitigations: Pause Airflow runs during manual editing
Use branch protection and required reviews
Separate automation output directories from source trees
Commit from one actor at a time
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace proposes edits for human review, but it still consumes repo context and can act on Airflow-produced artifacts. If Airflow emits incorrect facts or generated files, Copilot may propagate them into code or docs without independent verification. Human review reduces but does not eliminate the cascade, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Airflow outputs are treated as authoritative inputs to Copilot prompts or Workspace context
IF the human reviewer approves Copilot edits without checking upstream provenance
mitigations: Require source-of-truth checks before accepting edits
Annotate generated files as untrusted inputs
Review Airflow outputs separately from Copilot suggestions
Use tests to validate downstream changes
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show a clear residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Copilot does handle repo context through GitHub APIs, while Airflow’s profile does not specify regulated data classes, so there is no concrete compliance breach pathway to elevate beyond low. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but the evidence is thin.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into repositories or buffers indexed by Copilot
IF an external policy requires a residency or retention guarantee not shown in either profile
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared repos
Confirm retention and residency settings before use
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive projects
Document data-handling policy for the workspace
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations
